editorial.thesis: A motor-trade-and-learning city of about 2.5 million. Its retail is heavy on coaching & training and banks & atms, and thin on desserts, sweets & ice cream and restaurants & fast food — and 32% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 56% of Mumbai's. 13.27 chain outlets per lakh residents against 23.76 in Mumbai; 36 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by MedPlus 52, Apollo Pharmacy 45, Domino's 33.

The mapped economy leans to automotive. Shares of all mapped places: automotive 3.6% (Mumbai 2.2%); education 10.5% (Mumbai 7.5%); desserts & sweets 0.7% (Mumbai 1.1%); food & beverage 8.1% (Mumbai 10.1%). Raw counts would mislead because Mumbai is mapped more completely (70,423 places against 21,194), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 5 zones hold 32% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Mhalginagar alone has about 203,000 residents and 56 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is more concentrated than in Mumbai. 46% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Mumbai 38%). The largest cores are Shankar Nagar · Khare Town (1,584 places) and Patwardhan Ground · Sitabuldi (968).

The widest brand gaps against Mumbai. Café Coffee Day 26 outlets vs 169; Domino's 33 outlets vs 115; Subway 3 outlets vs 81. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Mumbai, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Mhalginagar and Uppalwadi are the largest zones by residents (203,000 and 197,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 46% of all commercial places, and Shankar Nagar · Khare Town alone lists 1,584.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Shankar Nagar · Khare Town holds 37 of the 331 tracked chain outlets, and Nagpur · Hanuman Nagar adds 22.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Shankar Nagar · Khare Town and Raje Raghujinagar · Ayodhya Nagar lead on education places (226 and 148, with 104 and 63 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Mhalginagar and Uppalwadi. The blue cores include Shankar Nagar · Khare Town.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (70,423 places in Mumbai against 21,194 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Mumbai; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Mumbai, Nagpur's mapped places over-index on automotive (3.6% vs 2.2%), education (10.5% vs 7.5%), healthcare (11.3% vs 8.7%) and under-index on desserts & sweets (0.7% vs 1.1%), food & beverage (8.1% vs 10.1%), grocery & daily needs (1.5% vs 1.9%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 331 outlets of 36 tracked national brands within 10 km — 13.27 per lakh residents against Mumbai's 23.76 (1266 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Mumbai are Café Coffee Day (26 vs 169); Domino's (33 vs 115); Subway (3 vs 81). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Mumbai's, so low means thin by Mumbai's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Nagpur's age mix against Mumbai: children (0–14) 21.9% vs 19.9%, 15–24 19.4% vs 19.7%, working age 49.2% vs 52.0%, 60+ 9.5% vs 8.4%. Under-25s are 41% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 5.5% of mapped places against 7.0% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 33 (Mumbai 115), Haldiram's 22 (Mumbai 5), Pizza Hut 11 (Mumbai 53), KFC 5 (Mumbai 38).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.5% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 26 (Mumbai 169), Chai Sutta Bar 3 (Mumbai 4), Starbucks 2 (Mumbai 64).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.7% of mapped places against 1.1% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 6 (Mumbai 57), Havmor 2 (Mumbai 11), Naturals 1 (Mumbai 18). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.5% of mapped places against 1.9% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 10 (Mumbai 18), DMart 4 (Mumbai 24), Big Bazaar 4 (Mumbai 8). No mapped outlet in either city: More, Vishal Mega Mart, Easyday.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.2% of mapped places against 1.3% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: MedPlus 52 (Mumbai 1), Apollo Pharmacy 45 (Mumbai 45), Wellness Forever 2 (Mumbai 17). No mapped outlet in either city: Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.5% of mapped places against 4.8% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 17 (Mumbai 52), Raymond 16 (Mumbai 40), Reliance Trends 11 (Mumbai 20), Tanishq 10 (Mumbai 32).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.4% of mapped places against 7.8% in Mumbai, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.8% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 4.0% of mapped places against 4.4% in Mumbai, so the mix is level.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
